$schema_note: parse_canonical test fixtures (Rust). Loaded by the Rust test suite (via `include_str!` in parse_canonical.rs's `shared_fixture_cases_match_expected` test). Each case describes an on-disk source tree (agents/skills/agent-sops) reconstructed from this file's `files` map (relative path -> content), then asserted against expected.ok (sorted agent/skill/sop names plus optional per-field skill assertions) or expected.error (field/reason_substring). `input.source_dir_is_file`, when true, tells the test harness to point parse_canonical at a plain file instead of the constructed tree (ignoring `files`). `input.skill_md_oversized`, when true, tells the test harness to write a real SKILL.md larger than MAX_AUXILIARY_FILE_BYTES under a synthesized skill directory instead of using `files` (a fixture-embedded 1MB+ string is impractical in JSON). Skill frontmatter is passed through verbatim (`skill_raw_frontmatter`): synth checks that `name` and `description` keys are present (key only, not either value's type -- the name actually used for path/validation is the skill's directory name, never the YAML-resolved value), so no scalar-shape (date, bool-word, numeral, ...) is rejected at parse time -- all such content round-trips as raw text.

cases.name: crlf_terminated_skill_md_strips_full_separator_and_matches_lf_body
cases.$comment: Regression fixture: a CRLF-terminated SKILL.md must not leave a stray '\r' at the frontmatter/body boundary. Rust's original `trim_start_matches('\n')` handled only LF, leaving a double-blank-line bug; the fix must strip '\r' alongside '\n' in both languages (mirroring the LF-only audit performed across the whole split_frontmatter path, not just one call site). `skill_body` here is intentionally CRLF throughout, matching the source file's line endings verbatim -- `fs::read_to_string` must preserve '\r' rather than one language silently normalizing it away via universal-newline translation.

cases.name: unindented_interior_dash_line_ends_frontmatter_early_in_both_runtimes
cases.$comment: split_frontmatter is line-based, not YAML-aware: an unindented line that is exactly '---' inside a folded scalar's continuation is treated as the CLOSING fence in both languages (matching how a real YAML loader also treats a column-0 '---' as a document separator), not as scalar content. Pins that both implementations draw the split at the same point rather than silently disagreeing on the frontmatter/body boundary.
